He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. Porter was ranked as one of the top prospects in the class of 2017.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Michael-Porter-34291|title=Michael Porter, Nathan Hale, Small Forward|website=247Sports}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/193628/michael-porter-jr|title=Michael Porter Jr. - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/373|title=Rivals.com|website=n.rivals.com|access-date=February 20, 2017|archive-date=April 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411105747/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/373|url-status=dead}} He was selected 14th overall by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], winning his first NBA championship with them in [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. After six seasons with Denver, Porter was traded to the Nets in 2025. ==Early life== Porter attended [[Father Tolton Regional Catholic High School]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]], before transferring to [[Nathan Hale High School (Washington)|Nathan Hale High School]] in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]], for his senior year. His father, Michael Porter Sr., was hired by the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|University of Washington]] to be an assistant coach; former NBA player [[Brandon Roy]] was the coach of Nathan Hale's basketball team.{{cite web | title=Michael Porter Jr., Jontay transfer to Nathan Hale (Seattle) to play for new coach Brandon Roy | website=USA Today High School Sports | date=2016-06-25 | url=https://www.usatodayhss.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/06/25/michael-porter-jr-brother-transfer-to-nathan-hale-seattle-to-play-for-new-coach-brandon-roy/77353502007/ | access-date=2025-07-06}}{{cite web|url=http://www.columbiatribune.com/sports/prep_sports/tolton/michael-and-jontay-porter-leaving-storied-high-school-careers-with/article_55b08978-034b-5b41-9b93-0dfdca56df1d.html|title=Michael and Jontay Porter leaving storied high school careers with move to Seattle|first=Daniel|last=Jones}} In Porter's junior season at Father Tolton, he led the team to the 3A State Championship.{{Cite web|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/prep_sports/tolton-boys-basketball-wins-first-state-championship/article_40622df4-e8a2-11e5-bd40-3be73ad670f6.html|title=Tolton boys basketball wins first state championship|last=Jarvis|first=Will|date=March 12, 2016|publisher=Columbia Missourian|access-date=January 7, 2019}} In the 2016 summer, Porter joined Mokan Elite on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) averaging 26.2 points and 11.5 rebounds per game leading them to the Nike EYBL Peach Jam championship and was named Co-MVP alongside teammate and future NBA player [[Trae Young]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/670158-peach-jam-2016-co-mvp-s-mokan-duo-trae-young-and-michael-porter-jr-|title=Peach Jam 2016 Co-MVP's: Mokan duo Trae Young & Michael Porter Jr|publisher=D1 Circuit|date=August 18, 2016|access-date=January 9, 2020}} In his senior season, Porter averaged 36.2 points and 13.6 rebounds as he helped his high school team earn a perfect 29–0 record and win the Washington Class 3A State Championship.{{Cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/nathan-hale-finishes-off-perfect-season-with-a-flourish-beating-garfield-for-class-3a-state-title/|title=Nathan Hale finishes off perfect season with a flourish, beating Garfield for Class 3A state title|last=Evans|first=Jayda|date=March 4, 2017|publisher=The Seattle Times|access-date=January 7, 2020}} He recorded 52 points and 23 rebounds in a blowout victory over [[Seattle Preparatory School|Seattle Prep]] on senior night.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/tuesday-high-school-results-michael-porter-scores-52-points-on-senior-night-as-nathan-hale-beats-seattle-prep/|title=Tuesday high school results: Nathan Hale crushes Seattle Prep as Michael Porter scores 52|publisher=[[Seattle Times]]|date=January 31, 2017|access-date=June 22, 2021}} Porter was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked as one of the top overall recruits in his class by [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]]. On March 29, 2017, Porter was named MVP at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] leading the West in a 109–107 win over the East team.{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/michael-porter-jr-wins-mvp-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game-victory|title=Michael Porter Jr wins MVP in McDonald's All-American Game Victory|last=Jordan|first=Jason|date=March 29, 2017|publisher=USA Today|access-date=January 7, 2020}} Porter also participated in the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], leading Team USA to a 98–87 victory over the World Select Team with 19 points in 23 minutes of play.{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|title=LiveStats - USA vs World Select Team - Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=April 8, 2017}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Michael Porter Jr. | position = SF | hometown = [[Columbia, Missouri|Columbia, MO]] | highschool = [[Nathan Hale High School (Washington)|Nathan Hale High School]] (WA) | feet = 6 | inches = 9 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = March 24, 2017 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | rivals ref title = https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/michael-porter-jr-373 | scout ref title = http://www.scout.com/Player/Michael-Porter-34291 | espn ref title = http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/193628/michael-porter-jr | rivals overall = 1 | scout overall = 2 | 247sports overall = 2 | espn overall = 2 }} ==College career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Michael Porter Jr. with the ball.jpg|thumb|Porter at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] In July 2016, Porter originally committed to Washington.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/17085923/top-recruit-michael-porter-jr-commits-play-washington-huskies|title=Top recruit Porter commits to play at Washington|date=July 15, 2016|website=ESPN.com}} After [[Lorenzo Romar]] was fired as Washington's head coach, Porter Sr. was hired as an assistant coach for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|University of Missouri]]. Porter Jr. later decommitted from Washington.{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article89974157.html|title=Top basketball recruit Michael Porter Jr. commits to Washington instead of MU, other finalists}} On March 24, 2017, Porter committed to play for Missouri, joining his father and his younger brother, [[Jontay Porter]] (who [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] from the class of 2018).{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18995284/no-1-prospect-michael-porter-jr-commits-missouri-tigers|title=No.1 prospect Michael Porter Jr commits to Missouri|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=March 24, 2017|publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 9, 2020}} Porter was injured in the first half of the season opener against Iowa State. Porter was expected to miss the remainder of the 2017–18 season because of a lower back injury which required surgery.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21505145/missouri-freshman-forward-michael-porter-jr-likely-miss-remainder-season|title=Michael Porter Jr. to have back surgery, likely out for rest of season|work=[[ESPN]]|author=ESPN Newswire|date=November 21, 2017|access-date=November 21, 2017}} On November 22, 2017, Porter had a successful microdiscectomy of his L3-L4 spinal discs.{{cite web|title=Porter Jr. Has Surgery|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/no-slam-dunk-michael-porters-back-surgery-plants-doubt-into-2018-nba-draft/|website=CBS Sports|date=November 22, 2017 |publisher=CBS}} On February 22, 2018, Porter Jr. was cleared to practice with Missouri again, with the potential to return to play before the end of the season. [[NBA]] executives were encouraging him to play if he was feeling healthy enough to do so.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/missouri-freshman-michael-porter-jr-cleared-for-all-basketball-activities/|title=Missouri freshman Michael Porter Jr. cleared for all basketball activities|last=Boone|first=Kyle|date=February 22, 2018|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=2019-05-27}} Porter would officially return to action on March 8, 2018, in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22694904/michael-porter-jr-not-especially-sharp-return-missouri-tigers|title=Michael Porter Jr. off in return from back surgery|work=[[ESPN]]|author=Alex Scarborough|date=March 8, 2018|access-date=March 8, 2018}} Porter would also play in the first round of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], where the team lost to [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. In both games, however, Porter came off the bench to play instead of starting as he had on opening night, mainly as a precaution. On March 27, Porter announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|first=Kyle |last=Boone|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2018-nba-draft-michael-porter-jr-declares-after-one-injury-plagued-year-at-missouri/|title=2018 NBA Draft: Michael Porter Jr. declares after one injury-plagued year at Missouri|work=cbssports.com.com|access-date= March 27, 2018|date=March 27, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2018–2025)=== Porter was selected with the 14th overall pick by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/23/report-denver-nuggets-draft-pick-michael-porter-jr-uncertain-summer-league |title=Report: Denver Nuggets draft pick Michael Porter Jr. uncertain for Summer League |date=June 23, 2018 |access-date=June 24, 2018 |publisher=NBA}} He fell from a possible first overall pick to the 14th pick with the Nuggets due to reports regarding his health.{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Scott |title=One of the top NBA prospects tumbled in the draft over fears about an injury and lost millions |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/michael-porter-jr-fell-draft-injury-lost-millions-2018-6 |website=Business Insider |access-date=July 24, 2018 |date=June 22, 2018}} The Nuggets also discussed the possibility of having him sit out for his entire first season in the NBA in relation to his back problems.{{cite web |title=Report: Denver Nuggets draft pick Michael Porter Jr. uncertain for Summer League |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/23/report-denver-nuggets-draft-pick-michael-porter-jr-uncertain-summer-league |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 24, 2018 |date=June 23, 2018}} On July 3, 2018, Porter signed a multi-year contract with the Nuggets.{{cite web |title=Denver Nuggets Sign Rookie Michael Porter Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-porter-jr-070318-2 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 4, 2018 |date=July 3, 2018}} On July 19, 2018, the Nuggets announced that Porter had undergone a second back surgery{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/michael-porter-jr-has-second-back-surgery-but-nuggets-dont-plan-to-sit-him-out-for-entire-season-report-says/|title=Michael Porter Jr. has second back surgery, but Nuggets don't plan to sit him out for entire season, report says|first=Colin|last= Ward-Henninger|date=Jul 19, 2018|access-date=March 26, 2019|work=CBSSports.com}} and subsequently missed the entire season. On October 31, 2019, Porter made his debut in the NBA, coming off the bench with fifteen points, four rebounds, and an assist in a 107–122 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160709|title=Pelicans beat Nuggets for first victory of season|date=October 31, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=November 1, 2019}} On December 29, he made his first career start in the NBA, finishing with 19 points, along with six rebounds and an assist in 26 minutes in a 120–115 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161131|title=Barton, Porter each score 19 as Nuggets beat Kings 120–115|date=December 29, 2019|work=www.ESPN.com|access-date=January 1, 2020}} He set a new career high with 25 points in 23 minutes just four days later in a win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161151|title=Nuggets use second-half rally to win at Indiana 124–116|date=January 2, 2020|work=www.ESPN.com|access-date=January 5, 2020}} On August 4, 2020, returning from the suspension of the season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Porter Jr. led the Nuggets to their first victory in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando bubble]], scoring a then career-high 37 points in route to a 121–113 overtime win over [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/michael-porter-jr-scores-career-high-37-to-lead-nuggets-to-critical-win-over-thunder-with-three-starters-out/|title=Michael Porter Jr. scores career-high 37 to lead Nuggets to critical win over Thunder with three starters out|website=CBSSports.com|date=August 4, 2020}} On April 24, 2021, Porter scored a career-high 39 points in a 129–116 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307711|title=Porter scores career-high 39 points, Nuggets beat Rockets|website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|date=April 24, 2021|access-date=April 26, 2021}} On September 27, 2021, Porter and the Denver Nuggets agreed to a 5-year, $172 million [[Derrick Rose Rule|rookie extension]] that will become $207 million if Porter is selected to an [[All-NBA Team]].{{Cite web|date=2021-09-27|title=Agent: Porter agrees to max deal with Nuggets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32293736/sources-michael-porter-jr-agrees-5-year-207m-max-extension-denver-nuggets|access-date=2021-10-23|website=ESPN.com}} He was expected to be the secondary scoring option behind [[Nikola Jokić]] while [[Jamal Murray]] continued to recover from a torn ACL.{{cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/2021/10/13/22723584/michael-porter-jr-denver-nuggets-covid-19 |title=Michael Porter Jr. Will Get His Moment … If He's Ready for It |website=The Ringer |date=October 13, 2021 |access-date=May 25, 2024}} On November 29, 2021, having appeared in only 9 games, Porter's agent Mark Bartelstein announced Porter would miss the remainder of the [[2021–22 NBA season]] as he would be undergoing a third back surgery.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/news/michael-porter-jr-back-surgery | title=Michael Porter Jr. Out indefinitely after lumbar spine surgery | website=[[NBA.com]]}} In Game 5 of the [[2023 NBA Finals]], Porter put up 16 points and 13 rebounds in a 94–89 win over the [[Miami Heat]] to help the Nuggets win their first NBA championship in franchise history.{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/nuggets-news-michael-porter-jr-message-to-critics-after-winning-nba-finals-despite-struggles|title=Nuggets forward Michael Porter Jr.'s message to critics after winning NBA Finals despite struggles|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=June 12, 2023|access-date=June 12, 2023}} On March 21, 2024, Porter put up 31 points along with his 193rd made three-pointer of the season, surpassing the previous record of 192 set by [[Dale Ellis]] for the most made three-pointers in a season in Nuggets franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nuggets-news-michael-porter-jr-sets-denver-franchise-3-point-record-in-win-over-knicks|title=Michael Porter Jr. sets Nuggets franchise 3-point record in win over Knicks|website=ClutchPoints|last=Strand|first=Rachel|date=March 23, 2024|access-date=March 23, 2024}} On November 10, 2024, Porter scored 17 points and hit the game-winning jumper in a 122–120 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401704774|title=Michael Porter Jr. hits winning jumper in the final seconds and Denver beats Dallas 122-120|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 10, 2024|accessdate=February 4, 2025}} On February 3, 2025, Porter had 36 points in a 125–113 win over the New Orleans Pelicans.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/4017052724|title=Nikola Jokic's 23rd triple-double of the season leads Nuggets over Pelicans 125-113|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=February 4, 2025|accessdate=February 4, 2025}} On February 5, Porter put up a career-high-tying 39 points, alongside 12 rebounds, in a 144–119 win over the New Orleans Pelicans.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nuggets-news-nikola-jokic-michael-porter-jr-nba-record-pelicans|title=Nuggets' Nikola Jokic, Michael Porter Jr. set NBA record in win vs. Pelicans|website=ClutchPoints|last=Finnegan|first=Troy|date=February 5, 2025|access-date=February 5, 2025}} The next day, Porter scored 30 points in 112–90 win over the [[Orlando Magic]]. He became the first player in Nuggets history to record three straight games of 30+ points and 5+ three-pointers.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-feb-7-2025-2 |title=Starting 5, Feb. 7: LeBron, Steph & a (new) all-time duel, Ant can't stop |date=February 7, 2025 |website=NBA.com}} === Brooklyn Nets (2025–present) === On July 8, 2025, Porter and a 2032 first-round draft pick were traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Cameron Johnson]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-michael-porter-jr|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Michael Porter Jr.|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2025|access-date=July 8, 2025}} He started 52 contests for Brooklyn during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 3.0 assists (all career-highs). On April 3, 2026, Porter was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to ankle and hamstring injuries.{{Cite web|title=Nets rule out Michael Porter Jr., Danny Wolf for remainder of season|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/nets-rule-michael-porter-jr-231701956.html|access-date=June 11, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2019}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2019–20 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 55 || 8 || 16.4 || .509 || .422 || .833 || 4.7 || .8 || .5 || .5 || 9.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2020}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2020–21 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 61 || 54 || 31.3 || '''.542''' || '''.445''' || .791 || '''7.3''' || 1.1 || .7 || '''.9''' || 19.0 |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2021–22 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]] | 9 || 9 || 29.5 || .359 || .208 || .556 || 6.6 || 1.9 || '''1.1''' || .2 || 9.9 |- | style="text-align:left; In 2018, he changed his diet to [[raw vegan]].{{cite web|first=Christopher|last=Cason|url=https://www.gq.com/story/michael-porter-jr-real-life-diet|date=May 23, 2018|title=The Real-Life Diet of Michael Porter Jr., Future NBA Lottery Pick and Raw Vegan|magazine=[[GQ]]|access-date=October 18, 2018}} As of 2020, Porter is no longer vegetarian or vegan.{{Cite news |last=Andrews |first=Kendra |title='It was just so good': Michael Porter Jr. never ate meat until … it's bacon! |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1670282/2020/03/13/it-was-just-so-good-michael-porter-jr-never-ate-meat-until-its-bacon/ |access-date=2023-05-19}} In addition to younger brother [[Jontay Porter|Jontay]], he has two older sisters named Bri and Cierra, along with four younger siblings.{{Cite
